1	# AI Persona Builder
     2	
     3	Build AI persona instruction files for **VS Code Chat**, **Claude Code** and **LangGraph Deep Agents** from YAML metadata and Markdown templates — with zero configuration friction.
     4	
     5	Define your personas once as simple YAML + Markdown sources, and the library generates correctly formatted instruction files for both IDEs. A plugin system lets you inject custom frontmatter, run validators, or post-process output without touching the core engine.
     6	
     7	## ✨ Features
     8	
     9	- **Multi-target output** — generates VS Code `.agent.md`, Claude Code `.md`, Deep Agents `.md`, and any custom format from a single source
    10	- **Extensible target registry** — register custom targets via `TargetRegistry` without touching core code; each target declares its own output key, frontmatter template, and context flags
    11	- **YAML + Markdown templating** — separate metadata from content; merge them at build time with `{{variables}}`, `{{> partials}}`, and `{{#if}}` conditionals
    12	- **Shared + per-suite partials** — reuse content fragments across personas with local overrides
    13	- **Custom variables** — inject global or per-suite template variables via `BuildConfig.variables` and `SuiteConfig.variables` without touching persona YAML files
    14	- **Dynamic partials** — supply inline partials via `BuildConfig.partials`, or override them at suite or per-persona level through the `onPartials` and `onPersonaPartials` plugin hooks
    15	- **Plugin architecture** — hook into context building, post-rendering, validation, and frontmatter generation
    16	- **CI-friendly** — `--check` mode renders without writing; `--strict` exits non-zero on warnings
    17	- **Programmatic & CLI** — use the `build()` API in scripts or run `persona-build` from the command line
    18	- **Single dependency** — only `js-yaml` at runtime
    19	
    20	## 📋 Requirements
    21	
    22	- **Node.js** ≥ 18
    23	
    24	## 🚀 Quick Start
    25	
    26	```bash
    27	npm install @mistralys/persona-builder
    28	```
    29	
    30	- View on NPM: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mistralys/persona-builder
    31	- View on Github: https://github.com/Mistralys/ai-persona-builder
    32	
    33	### Programmatic API
    34	
    35	```ts
    36	import { build } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
    37	import path from 'node:path';
    38	
    39	const summary = await build({
    40	  suites: {
    41	    'my-suite': {
    42	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/my-suite'),
    43	      outputDirs: {
    44	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/vscode'),
    45	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/claude-code'),
    46	      },
    47	    },
    48	  },
    49	  sharedPartialsDir: path.resolve('./personas/shared/partials'),
    50	});
    51	
    52	console.log(`Built ${summary.totalBuilt} persona(s), wrote ${summary.totalWritten} file(s).`);
    53	```
    54	
    55	### CLI
    56	
    57	```bash
    58	# Create a persona-build.config.js, then:
    59	npx persona-build
    60	
    61	# CI staleness check
    62	npx persona-build --check --strict
    63	```
    64	
    65	See the [CLI docs](docs/cli.md) for config file format and all flags.
    66	
    67	## 📖 Documentation
    68	
    69	**Guides** — conceptual and procedural reading:
    70	
    71	| Guide | Description |
    72	|-------|-------------|
    73	| [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md) | Step-by-step tutorial — build your first persona from scratch |
    74	| [Directory Convention](docs/directory-convention.md) | Expected source layout (`meta/`, `content/`, `partials/`) |
    75	| [Template Syntax](docs/template-syntax.md) | Variables, partials, conditionals, and built-in context variables |
    76	| [Custom Variables & Dynamic Partials](docs/dynamic-partials.md) | Inject build-time variables and partial content at global, suite, or per-persona level |
    77	| [Plugins](docs/plugins.md) | `PersonaBuildPlugin` interface and examples |
    78	
    79	**Reference** — look-up material:
    80	
    81	| Reference | Description |
    82	|-----------|-------------|
    83	| [Metadata Reference](docs/metadata-reference.md) | All recognized YAML metadata fields, tiers, and fallback rules |
    84	| [Configuration Reference](docs/configuration.md) | `BuildConfig`, `SuiteConfig`, and `BuildSummary` fields |
    85	| [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Command-line flags, config file format, and common patterns |
    86	| [Public API](docs/api.md) | All exported types and functions |
    87	| [Project Manifest](docs/agents/project-manifest/README.md) | Canonical documentation for AI agent sessions |
    88	
    89	## 🔌 Plugins
    90	
    91	The library ships with a plugin system that lets you inject custom frontmatter, run validators, or
    92	post-process output without touching the core engine. See [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md) for
    93	the `PersonaBuildPlugin` interface, examples, and the available hooks.
    94	
    95	> **Ledger plugin:** The first-party ledger plugin was migrated out of this library in v2.0.0 and
    96	> is now maintained in the [ai-insights](https://github.com/mistralys/ai-insights-dev) workspace.
    97	> The `@mistralys/persona-builder/plugins/ledger` sub-path export no longer exists.
    98

1	# Custom Variables & Dynamic Partials
     2	
     3	This guide covers two complementary mechanisms for injecting build-time content that varies
     4	across projects, suites, or individual personas:
     5	
     6	- **Custom variables** — inject template values via `BuildConfig.variables` and `SuiteConfig.variables`
     7	- **Dynamic partials** — inject or override partial content via `BuildConfig.partials`, `onPartials` and `onPersonaPartials` plugin hooks
     8	
     9	Both features follow the same design principle: **later layers win**. Values defined closer to the
    10	individual persona always take precedence over those defined at the global level.
    11	
    12	---
    13	
    14	## Table of Contents
    15	
    16	1. [Custom Variables](#1-custom-variables)
    17	   - [Level 1 — Global variables via `BuildConfig.variables`](#level-1--global-variables-via-buildconfigvariables)
    18	   - [Level 2 — Per-suite variables via `SuiteConfig.variables`](#level-2--per-suite-variables-via-suiteconfigvariables)
    19	   - [Variables merge/override order](#variables-mergeoverride-order)
    20	2. [Dynamic Partials](#2-dynamic-partials)
    21	   - [Level 1 — Inline partials via `BuildConfig.partials`](#level-1--inline-partials-via-buildconfigpartials)
    22	   - [Level 2 — Suite-scoped overrides via the `onPartials` plugin hook](#level-2--suite-scoped-overrides-via-the-onpartials-plugin-hook)
    23	   - [Level 3 — Per-persona overrides via the `onPersonaPartials` plugin hook](#level-3--per-persona-overrides-via-the-onpersonapartials-plugin-hook)
    24	   - [Partials merge/override order](#partials-mergeoverride-order)
    25	3. [Combining variables and partials](#3-combining-variables-and-partials)
    26	
    27	---
    28	
    29	## 1. Custom Variables
    30	
    31	Custom variables let you inject arbitrary key/value pairs into the template context from outside
    32	the YAML metadata files. They are ideal for values that are known at build time but should not
    33	live inside the persona source files — for example, project-wide environment names, base URLs,
    34	or shared configuration tokens.
    35	
    36	### Level 1 — Global variables via `BuildConfig.variables`
    37	
    38	Set `variables` on the top-level `BuildConfig` to make values available to every persona across
    39	all suites.
    40	
    41	```ts
    42	import { build } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
    43	import path from 'node:path';
    44	
    45	await build({
    46	  suites: {
    47	    'engineering': {
    48	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/engineering'),
    49	      outputDirs: {
    50	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/engineering/vscode'),
    51	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/engineering/claude-code'),
    52	      },
    53	    },
    54	    'support': {
    55	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/support'),
    56	      outputDirs: {
    57	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/support/vscode'),
    58	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/support/claude-code'),
    59	      },
    60	    },
    61	  },
    62	
    63	  // Available in every template in every suite:
    64	  variables: {
    65	    company_name: 'Acme Corp',
    66	    support_email: 'help@acme.example',
    67	    environment: 'production',
    68	  },
    69	});
    70	```
    71	
    72	Any template in any suite can then reference these variables:
    73	
    74	```md
    75	## Contact
    76	
    77	Reach the {{company_name}} team at {{support_email}}.
    78	```
    79	
    80	### Level 2 — Per-suite variables via `SuiteConfig.variables`
    81	
    82	Set `variables` on a `SuiteConfig` entry to inject values that apply only to that suite. These
    83	override any same-named global variable from `BuildConfig.variables`.
    84	
    85	```ts
    86	await build({
    87	  suites: {
    88	    'engineering': {
    89	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/engineering'),
    90	      outputDirs: {
    91	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/engineering/vscode'),
    92	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/engineering/claude-code'),
    93	      },
    94	
    95	      // Override company_name for this suite only:
    96	      variables: {
    97	        company_name: 'Acme Engineering',
    98	        on_call_channel: '#eng-oncall',
    99	      },
   100	    },

   122	
   123	The `engineering` suite will render `{{company_name}}` as `"Acme Engineering"`, while the
   124	`support` suite will render it as `"Acme Corp"`.
   125	
   126	### Variables merge/override order
   127	
   128	Template variables are built from seven layers. **Later layers always win over earlier ones**:
   129	
   130	| Layer | Source | Priority |
   131	|-------|--------|----------|
   132	| 1 | `BuildConfig.variables` | Lowest |
   133	| 2 | `SuiteConfig.variables` | — |
   134	| 3 | `_shared.yaml` fields | — |
   135	| 4 | Per-persona YAML fields | — |
   136	| 5 | Derived/computed fields (`version`, `tools_list`, etc.) | — |
   137	| 6 | Cross-suite agent map (`agent_<slug>` variables) | — |
   138	| 7 | Target flags (`target_vscode`, `target_claude_code`, etc.) | **Highest** |
   139	
   140	> **Key rule:** `SuiteConfig.variables` overrides `BuildConfig.variables`, but is itself
   141	> overridden by `_shared.yaml` fields and per-persona YAML metadata. Use `BuildConfig.variables`
   142	> for project-wide defaults and `SuiteConfig.variables` for suite-specific defaults.
   143	
   144	For example, if `BuildConfig.variables` sets `env: 'production'` and a persona's YAML also sets
   145	`env: 'staging'`, the persona's YAML value wins.
   146	
   147	See [Template Syntax → Variables](template-syntax.md#variables) for the full reference.
   148	
   149	---
   150	
   151	## 2. Dynamic Partials
   152	
   153	Dynamic partials let you inject or override partial content without placing files on disk. They
   154	are useful for programmatically generated content, environment-specific snippets, and per-persona
   155	content that depends on runtime data.
   156	
   157	### Level 1 — Inline partials via `BuildConfig.partials`
   158	
   159	Pass an inline `partials` map to `BuildConfig` to register partial content as strings. This is
   160	the simplest approach when you want to inject content that is computed at build time.
   161	
   162	```ts
   163	import { build } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
   164	import path from 'node:path';
   165	import fs from 'node:fs';
   166	
   167	// Example: load a dynamically generated partial from an external source
   168	const changelogSnippet = fs.readFileSync('./CHANGELOG.md', 'utf8')
   169	  .split('\n')
   170	  .slice(0, 10)           // Take just the first 10 lines
   171	  .join('\n');
   172	
   173	await build({
   174	  suites: {
   175	    'my-suite': {
   176	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/my-suite'),
   177	      outputDirs: {
   178	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/vscode'),
   179	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/claude-code'),
   180	      },
   181	    },
   182	  },
   183	
   184	  // Inline partials — lowest precedence layer:
   185	  partials: {
   186	    recent_changes: changelogSnippet,
   187	    legal_footer: '> © 2025 Acme Corp. All rights reserved.',
   188	  },
   189	});
   190	```
   191	
   192	Templates reference them the same way as file-based partials:
   193	
   194	```md
   195	## Recent Changes
   196	
   197	{{> recent_changes}}
   198	
   199	---
   200	
   201	{{> legal_footer}}
   202	```
   203	
   204	> **Note:** Inline partials from `BuildConfig.partials` are the **lowest-precedence** layer. Any
   205	> partial with the same name loaded from `sharedPartialsDir`, suite-local `partials/`, or an
   206	> `onPartials` hook will override them.
   207	
   208	### Level 2 — Suite-scoped overrides via the `onPartials` plugin hook
   209	
   210	The `onPartials` hook runs once per suite, after all partials are loaded from disk and after any
   211	`BuildConfig.partials` map has been merged in. Use it to inject or override partials
   212	programmatically at the suite level.
   213	
   214	**Contract:** receive the accumulated partials map, return the (possibly mutated) map. The
   215	returned map is passed to the next plugin in the chain. **Always include all original keys** —
   216	return `{ ...partialsMap, myPartial: '...' }` rather than a fresh object.
   217	
   218	```ts
   219	import type { PersonaBuildPlugin } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
   220	
   221	export const environmentBannerPlugin: PersonaBuildPlugin = {
   222	  name: 'environment-banner',
   223	
   224	  onPartials(partialsMap, suiteName, suite) {
   225	    // Inject an environment-specific banner for every persona in this suite.
   226	    const env = process.env.BUILD_ENV ?? 'development';
   227	
   228	    return {
   229	      ...partialsMap,
   230	      env_banner: env === 'production'
   231	        ? '> ⚠️ **Production environment.** Treat all data as live.'
   232	        : `> 🔧 **${env} environment.** Safe to experiment.`,
   233	    };
   234	  },
   235	};
   236	
   237	await build({
   238	  suites: {
   239	    'my-suite': {
   240	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/my-suite'),
   241	      outputDirs: {
   242	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/vscode'),
   243	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/claude-code'),
   244	      },
   245	    },
   246	  },
   247	  plugins: [environmentBannerPlugin],
   248	});
   249	```

251	> **Execution order:** Multiple plugins are chained — each receives the map returned by the
   252	> previous plugin. The order of `plugins` in `BuildConfig` controls which plugin runs first.
   253	> The **last** plugin to set a key wins.
   254	
   255	### Level 3 — Per-persona overrides via the `onPersonaPartials` plugin hook
   256	
   257	The `onPersonaPartials` hook runs once per persona (and per target), after `onBuildContext`.
   258	It receives a **shallow copy** of the suite-level partials map, so changes are isolated to the
   259	current persona — they will not affect other personas in the same suite.
   260	
   261	Use this hook when partial content depends on persona-specific data: role, tier, capabilities, or
   262	any field from the persona's YAML metadata.
   263	
   264	**Contract:** same chaining rules as `onPartials` — receive the map, return a new map. Mutating
   265	in place may work but is not guaranteed to be safe; always return `{ ...partialsMap, ... }`.
   266	
   267	```ts
   268	import type { PersonaBuildPlugin } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
   269	
   270	export const tierDisclaimerPlugin: PersonaBuildPlugin = {
   271	  name: 'tier-disclaimer',
   272	
   273	  onPersonaPartials(partialsMap, persona, context, suite, target) {
   274	    // `context` holds the post-onBuildContext merged state — all YAML fields
   275	    // and any keys injected by earlier onBuildContext plugins are accessible.
   276	    const tier = context['tier'] as string | undefined;
   277	
   278	    if (tier === 'admin') {
   279	      return {
   280	        ...partialsMap,
   281	        disclaimer: '> 🔒 **Admin persona.** Restricted to authorised users.',
   282	      };
   283	    }
   284	
   285	    if (tier === 'read-only') {
   286	      return {
   287	        ...partialsMap,
   288	        disclaimer: '> 👁️ **Read-only persona.** No write operations permitted.',
   289	      };
   290	    }
   291	
   292	    // Return unchanged map for personas without a tier field:
   293	    return partialsMap;
   294	  },
   295	};
   296	```
   297	
   298	A persona with `tier: admin` in its YAML will receive the admin disclaimer, while all other
   299	personas in the same suite receive the map untouched.
   300	
   301	```yaml
   302	# personas/my-suite/meta/admin-agent.yaml
   303	name: Admin Agent
   304	tier: admin
   305	vs_file_name: admin-agent.agent.md
   306	cc_file_name: admin-agent.md
   307	```
   308	
   309	The content template can then unconditionally include the partial:
   310	
   311	```md
   312	{{> disclaimer}}
   313	
   314	## Role
   315	
   316	...
   317	```
   318	
   319	Because `onPersonaPartials` runs per-persona, the `disclaimer` partial resolves to different
   320	content for each persona without any `{{#if}}` conditionals in the template itself.
   321	
   322	> **Isolation guarantee:** The builder shallow-copies the suite-level partials map before passing
   323	> it to the first `onPersonaPartials` plugin in the chain. Changes you apply inside this hook
   324	> are invisible to other personas in the same suite.
   325	
   326	### Partials merge/override order
   327	
   328	Partials are resolved in four layers. **Later layers always win over earlier ones**:
   329	
   330	| Layer | Source | Priority |
   331	|-------|--------|----------|
   332	| 1 | `BuildConfig.partials` (inline map) | Lowest |
   333	| 2 | `sharedPartialsDir` — files in the shared partials directory | — |
   334	| 3 | Suite-local partials — files in `<srcDir>/partials/` | — |
   335	| 4 | `onPartials` plugin hooks — plugin-injected partials | **Highest** |
   336	
   337	For per-persona rendering, an additional **copy** of the layer-4 map is handed to
   338	`onPersonaPartials` hooks, which can further override it for the duration of a single persona's
   339	render pass.
   340	
   341	> **Key rule:** `onPartials` hooks win over any file on disk. `onPersonaPartials` hooks win over
   342	> `onPartials` for the individual persona — but those overrides do not propagate back to the
   343	> suite-level map.
   344	
   345	---
   346	
   347	## 3. Combining variables and partials
   348	
   349	Variables and partials compose naturally. A partial injected by `onPersonaPartials` can itself
   350	reference template variables, and those variables are resolved in the normal 7-layer merge after
   351	all partials have been resolved.
   352	
   353	```ts
   354	// Plugin: inject a partial that references a template variable
   355	export const signaturePlugin: PersonaBuildPlugin = {
   356	  name: 'signature',
   357	
   358	  onPersonaPartials(partialsMap, persona, context) {
   359	    // The partial content can use {{variable}} syntax —
   360	    // variable substitution runs after partial inclusion.
   361	    return {
   362	      ...partialsMap,
   363	      signature: '— {{name}} v{{version}}, brought to you by {{company_name}}',
   364	    };
   365	  },
   366	};
   367	```
   368	
   369	Processing order for a template that includes `{{> signature}}`:
   370	
   371	1. `{{> signature}}` is replaced with the partial's raw content string.
   372	2. Template conditionals (`{{#if … }}`) are evaluated.
   373	3. `{{name}}`, `{{version}}`, and `{{company_name}}` are substituted from the merged context.
   374	
   375	This means you can author generic, reusable partial templates that are parameterised by context
   376	variables — the combination lets you express sophisticated per-persona content without hard-coding
   377	anything in the plugin itself.
   378	
   379	---
   380

   382	
   383	- [Configuration Reference](configuration.md) — `BuildConfig.variables`, `SuiteConfig.variables`, `BuildConfig.partials`

   385	- [Template Syntax](template-syntax.md) — variable substitution and partial inclusion

* partials.ts\n *\n * Pure template-engine function for resolving partial inclusions.\n * Supports {{> name}} syntax with up to depth-2 recursion to handle\n * partials-within-partials. No file-system I/O.\n */\n\n/**\n * Resolve partial inclusions in a template string.\n *\n * Replaces `{{> name}}` markers with the content from `partialsMap`.\n * Recursion is capped at depth 2 so that:\n *   - depth 0 → 1: outer partials are expanded\n *   - depth 1 → 2: one level of nested partials are expanded\n *   - depth 2: recursion stops, marker is left as-is\n *\n * Each resolved partial is `trimEnd()`-ed to prevent trailing blank lines\n * from causing double-blank-line artefacts during concatenation.\n *\n * If a partial name is not found in `partialsMap`, the original marker is\n * preserved and a warning is emitted via `console.warn`.\n *\n * @param text       - Template string potentially containing {{> name}} markers\n * @param partialsMap - Map of partial name → partial content\n * @param depth      - Current recursion depth (callers should omit; defaults to 0)\n * @returns          The template string with partial markers replaced\n */\nexport function resolvePartials(\n  text: string,\n  partialsMap: Record<string, string>,\n  depth = 0,\n): string {\n  if (depth >= 2) return text;\n  return text.replace(/\\{\\{> ([\\w-]+)\\}\\}/g, (match, name: string) => {\n    if (!(name in partialsMap)) {\n      console.warn(`[WARN] Partial not found: ${match}`);\n      return match;\n    }\n    // Recursively resolve nested partials (depth + 1).\n    // trimEnd() strips trailing whitespace to avoid extra blank lines.\n    return resolvePartials(partialsMap[name], partialsMap, depth + 1).trimEnd();\n  });\n}\n","/**\n * conditionals.ts\n *\n * Pure template-engine function for resolving conditional blocks.\n * Handles {{#if flag}}…{{/if}}, {{#if flag}}…{{else}}…{{/if}}, and\n * {{#if flag}}…{{else if flag2}}…{{else}}…{{/if}} (chain) syntax,\n * including nested {{#if}} blocks inside {{else}} branches.\n * No file-system I/O.\n */\n\n/**\n * Negative-lookahead fragment that matches any character sequence containing\n * no `{{#if` opener. Used as a shared building-block in the regex patterns of\n * both `resolveElseIf` and `resolveConditionals` so the two guards stay in sync.\n * @internal\n */\nconst NO_NESTED_IF = String.raw`(?:(?!\\{\\{#if\\b)[\\s\\S])*?`;\n\n/**\n * Matches `{{else if flag}}…{{/if}}` segments whose content contains no\n * nested `{{#if` opener. Hoisted to module level to avoid constructing a new\n * `RegExp` object on every `resolveElseIf()` call.\n * `String.prototype.replace()` resets `lastIndex` to 0 before each call, so\n * the shared `g`-flag instance is safe for repeated use.\n * @internal\n */\nconst ELSE_IF_PATTERN = new RegExp(\n  String.raw`\\{\\{else if (\\w+)\\}\\}(${NO_NESTED_IF})\\{\\{\\/if\\}\\}`,\n  'g',\n);\n\n/**\n * Pre-process `{{else if flag}}` chains by rewriting each innermost\n * occurrence into an equivalent nested `{{else}}{{#if flag}}` block.\n *\n * Examples:\n *   `{{#if a}}A{{else if b}}B{{else}}C{{/if}}`\n *   → `{{#if a}}A{{else}}{{#if b}}B{{else}}C{{/if}}{{/if}}`\n *\n * Multi-level chains are normalised iteratively, one level per pass:\n *   `{{#if a}}A{{else if b}}B{{else if c}}C{{/if}}`\n *   pass 1 → `{{#if a}}A{{else}}{{#if b}}B{{else if c}}C{{/if}}{{/if}}`\n *   pass 2 → `{{#if a}}A{{else}}{{#if b}}B{{else}}{{#if c}}C{{/if}}{{/if}}{{/if}}`\n *\n * The pattern matches only segments whose content contains no nested\n * `{{#if` markers, mirroring the innermost-first invariant of\n * `resolveConditionals`. This ensures `{{else if}}` chains that are\n * themselves nested inside outer `{{#if}}…{{else}}…{{/if}}` blocks are\n * handled safely.\n *\n * @internal\n */\nfunction resolveElseIf(text: string): string {\n  if (!text.includes('{{else if ')) {\n    return text;\n  }\n  // Use the module-level ELSE_IF_PATTERN constant. replace() resets the\n  // regex's lastIndex before each call, so sharing the instance is safe.\n  let result = text;\n  let prev: string;\n  do {\n    prev = result;\n    result = result.replace(\n      ELSE_IF_PATTERN,\n      (_match: string, flag: string, content: string): string =>\n        `{{else}}{{#if ${flag}}}${content}{{/if}}{{/if}}`,\n    );\n  } while (result !== prev);\n  return result;\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve conditional blocks in a template string.\n *\n * Syntax:\n *   `{{#if flag}}content{{/if}}`\n *   `{{#if flag}}truthy-content{{else}}falsy-content{{/if}}`\n *   `{{#if flag}}truthy-content{{else if flag2}}branch2{{else}}falsy-content{{/if}}`\n *\n * Nested conditionals inside `{{else}}` branches are supported:\n *   `{{#if a}}A{{else}}{{#if b}}B{{else}}C{{/if}}{{/if}}`\n *\n * `{{else if}}` chains are normalised into nested `{{#if}}` blocks before\n * resolution, so they work transparently alongside — and can be combined\n * with — traditional nested `{{#if}}` syntax.\n *\n * Behaviour:\n * - When `context[flag]` is truthy: the delimiters are stripped and the\n *   content before `{{else}}` (or the entire inner block if no `{{else}}`)\n *   is kept, surrounded by single `\\n` delimiters.\n * - When `context[flag]` is falsy and a `{{else}}` branch exists: the\n *   content after `{{else}}` is kept, surrounded by single `\\n` delimiters.\n * - When `context[flag]` is falsy and no `{{else}}` branch exists: the\n *   entire block (including surrounding newlines) is removed, leaving a\n *   single `\\n`.\n * - Unknown flags (absent from context) are treated as falsy.\n *\n * Leading and trailing newlines within the kept content are trimmed so the\n * output does not accumulate extra blank lines.\n *\n * Nesting algorithm: the regex matches only *innermost* blocks — those\n * whose content contains no further `{{#if` markers. The replacement loop\n * repeats until the output stabilises, resolving each nesting level in\n * depth-first (innermost-first) order. This avoids the closing `{{/if}}`\n * ambiguity that arises with non-greedy single-pass matching.\n *\n * @param text    - Template string potentially containing {{#if}} blocks\n * @param context - Key-value map used to evaluate flag truthiness\n * @returns       The template string with conditional blocks resolved\n */\nexport function resolveConditionals(\n  text: string,\n  context: Record<string, unknown>,\n): string {\n  // Normalise {{else if}} chains into nested {{else}}{{#if}} blocks so the\n  // existing innermost-first resolution loop handles them transparently.\n  const normalized = resolveElseIf(text);\n\n  // Match only innermost conditional blocks — those whose truthy and falsy\n  // content contains no nested `{{#if`. The negative lookahead\n  // `(?!\\{\\{#if\\b)` ensures the quantifier stops before any nested opener,\n  // so each pass resolves one depth level. Subsequent passes bubble outward\n  // until the output stabilises (no more `{{#if` markers remain).\n  const pattern = new RegExp(\n    String.raw`\\n*\\{\\{#if (\\w+)\\}\\}(${NO_NESTED_IF})` +\n      String.raw`(?:\\{\\{else\\}\\}(${NO_NESTED_IF}))?\\{\\{\\/if\\}\\}\\n*`,\n    'g',\n  );\n\n  const resolve = (\n    _match: string,\n    flag: string,\n    inner: string,\n    elseInner: string | undefined,\n  ): string => {\n    if (context[flag]) {\n      // Truthy: keep content before {{else}} (or entire inner if no {{else}})\n      return '\\n' + inner.replace(/^\\n+/, '').replace(/\\n+$/, '') + '\\n';\n    }\n    if (elseInner !== undefined) {\n      // Falsy with {{else}}: keep content after {{else}}\n      return '\\n' + elseInner.replace(/^\\n+/, '').replace(/\\n+$/, '') + '\\n';\n    }\n    // Falsy without {{else}}: remove entire block\n    return '\\n';\n  };\n\n  let result = normalized;\n  let prev: string;\n  do {\n    prev = result;\n    result = result.replace(pattern, resolve);\n  } while (result !== prev);\n  return result;\n}\n","/**\n * variables.ts\n *\n * Pure template-engine function for resolving variable substitutions.\n * Handles {{varName}} syntax. No file-system I/O.\n */\n\n/**\n * Resolve variable substitutions in a template string.\n *\n * Replaces `{{varName}}` markers with `String(context[varName])`.\n * If a variable is not found in `context` (or its value is `undefined`),\n * the original marker is preserved and a warning is emitted via\n * `console.warn`, identifying the file by `filename` for easier debugging.\n *\n * Note: this step must run AFTER `resolvePartials` and `resolveConditionals`\n * so that only plain variable markers remain.\n *\n * @param text     - Template string potentially containing {{varName}} markers\n * @param context  - Key-value map of variable name → value\n * @param filename - Identifier used in warning messages (e.g. persona file path)\n * @returns        The template string with variable markers substituted\n */\nexport function resolveVariables(\n  text: string,\n  context: Record<string, unknown>,\n  filename: string,\n): string {\n  return text.replace(/\\{\\{(\\w+)\\}\\}/g, (match, varName: string) => {\n    if (varName in context && context[varName] !== undefined) {\n      return String(context[varName]);\n    }\n    console.warn(`[WARN] Unresolved variable: ${match} in ${filename}`);\n    return match;\n  });\n}\n","/**\n * postProcessor.ts\n *\n * Pure post-processing functions for cleaning up rendered persona output.\n * All functions are side-effect-free and operate only on strings.\n * No file-system I/O.\n */\n\n/**\n * Collapse 3 or more consecutive blank lines into 2 blank lines.\n *\n * Specifically converts 4 or more consecutive `\\n` characters into `\\n\\n\\n`\n * (which equals 2 blank lines between paragraphs).\n *\n * @param text - Rendered output string\n * @returns    String with excessive blank lines collapsed\n */\nexport function collapseBlankLines(text: string): string {\n  return text.replace(/\\n{4,}/g, '\\n\\n\\n');\n}\n\n/**\n * Ensure every Markdown heading has a blank line immediately before it.\n *\n * Also ensures horizontal rules (`---`) have a blank line before and after\n * them. This corrects spacing gaps caused by partial concatenation where\n * `trimEnd()` strips trailing newlines and conditionals add only a single\n * `\\n` delimiter.\n *\n * @param text - Rendered output string\n * @returns    String with blank lines inserted before headings and rules\n */\nexport function ensureBlankLineBeforeHeadings(text: string): string {\n  // Blank line before headings\n  let result = text.replace(/([^\\n])\\n(#{1,6} )/g, '$1\\n\\n$2');\n  // Blank line before horizontal rules (---)\n  result = result.replace(/([^\\n])\\n(---)\\n/g, '$1\\n\\n$2\\n');\n  // Blank line after horizontal rules (---)\n  result = result.replace(/\\n(---)\\n([^\\n])/g, '\\n$1\\n\\n$2');\n  return result;\n}\n\n/**\n * Normalize line endings to LF (`\\n`) for OS-agnostic output.\n *\n * Converts CRLF (`\\r\\n`) first, then strips any remaining stray CR (`\\r`).\n *\n * @param text - String potentially containing CRLF or CR line endings\n * @returns    String with all line endings normalized to LF\n */\nexport function normalizeNewlines(text: string): string {\n  return text.replace(/\\r\\n/g, '\\n').replace(/\\r/g, '\\n');\n}\n","/**\n * serializer.ts\n *\n * Pure serializer functions for converting tool lists to YAML-compatible\n * string representations. No file-system I/O.\n */\n\n/**\n * Serialize a tools array in YAML single-quote flow format WITH outer brackets.\n *\n * Output format: `['tool1', 'tool2', 'tool3']`\n * Used by the ledger suite to preserve byte-identical frontmatter output.\n *\n * @param tools - Array of tool name strings\n * @returns     YAML flow-sequence string including outer brackets\n *\n * @example\n * serializeTools(['Bash', 'Read']) // => \"['Bash', 'Read']\"\n * serializeTools([])              // => \"[]\"\n */\nexport function serializeTools(tools: string[]): string {\n  return '[' + tools.map((t) => `'${t}'`).join(', ') + ']';\n}\n\n/**\n * Serialize a tools array in YAML single-quote flow format WITHOUT outer brackets.\n *\n * Output format: `'tool1', 'tool2', 'tool3'`\n * Used inside standalone frontmatter templates which supply the surrounding `[ ]`.\n *\n * @param tools - Array of tool name strings\n * @returns     Comma-separated quoted tool names (no outer brackets)\n *\n * @example\n * serializeToolsList(['Bash', 'Read']) // => \"'Bash', 'Read'\"\n * serializeToolsList([])              // => \"\"\n */\nexport function serializeToolsList(tools: string[]): string {\n  return tools.map((t) => `'${t}'`).join(', ');\n}\n","/**\n * src/loaders/partials-loader.ts\n *\n * File-system loader for Handlebars-style partial snippets.\n *\n * Reads every `.md` file in `dir`, keys each entry by the filename stem\n * (i.e. the portion before the final `.md` extension), and returns the\n * map.  Callers that need a two-layer (shared → suite-local override)\n * setup should call `loadPartials` twice and merge the results themselves,\n * with the suite-local result spreading last.\n *\n * All file reads are performed asynchronously.  Path construction uses\n * `path.join` and `path.posix`-compatible operations so no path-separator\n * assumptions are baked in.\n */\n\nimport { readdir, readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport path from 'node:path';\n\n/**\n * Load all `.md` files in `dir` and return them as a `Record<string, string>`\n * keyed by filename stem.\n *\n * Files whose names do not end in `.md` are silently ignored.\n * The directory must exist; a missing directory throws an `ENOENT` error from\n * the underlying `readdir` call (let callers decide how to handle absence).\n *\n * @param dir  Absolute (or relative) path to the directory to scan.\n * @returns    A map from filename stem → file content string.\n *\n * @example\n * const partials = await loadPartials('/project/partials');\n * // { greeting: 'Hello, {{name}}!', footer: '---\\nEnd of file' }\n */\nexport async function loadPartials(dir: string): Promise<Record<string, string>> {\n  const entries = await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true });\n\n  const mdFiles = entries.filter(\n    (entry) => entry.isFile() && entry.name.endsWith('.md'),\n  );\n\n  const pairs = await Promise.all(\n    mdFiles.map(async (entry) => {\n      const stem = entry.name.slice(0, -'.md'.length); // strip trailing \".md\"\n      const filePath = path.join(dir, entry.name);\n      const content = await readFile(filePath, 'utf8');\n      return [stem, content] as [string, string];\n    }),\n  );\n\n  return Object.fromEntries(pairs);\n}\n","/**\n * src/plugins/runner.ts\n *\n * Plugin runner — responsible for invoking plugin hooks in registration order.\n *\n * Each exported function corresponds to one lifecycle hook defined in\n * PersonaBuildPlugin. The runner:\n *   - Skips plugins that do not implement the requested hook (hook is optional)\n *   - Invokes hooks in the order plugins are registered (first-in first-called)\n *   - For accumulating hooks (onBuildContext, onPartials, onPersonaPartials,\n *     onPostRender), each plugin receives the output of the previous plugin\n *     as its first argument\n *   - For collecting hooks (onValidate), results are concatenated into a\n *     flat array\n *\n * No file-system I/O.
